name: Question 10
problem:
Consider the following differential equation.

$$
2x{y}^{″}+{y}^{′}-5y=0
$$

The general solution near $x=0$ of the differential equation is given by

$$
y={c}_{1}{y}_{1}(x)+{c}_{2}{y}_{2}(x),
$$

where ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ are arbitrary constants and ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)$ are linearly independent solutions. According to the Frobenius method, what is the missing coefficient in the first solution ${y}_{1}?$

*Hint: You may assume $x=0$ is a regular singular point of the ODE, the indicial equation of the ODE is $2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda =0,$ and the recurrence relation for the coefficients is

$$
{a}_{n}(\lambda )=\frac{5}{(\lambda +n)(2(\lambda +n)-1)}\,{a}_{n-1}.
$$

*

The first solution is 

${y}_{1}(x)={a}_{0}({x}^{1/2}+\frac{5}{3}{x}^{3/2}\,+$ {{field-1}} ${x}^{5/2}+⋯).$
worked_solution:
The general solution near a regular singular point $x=0$ of a second-order homogeneous linear differential equation with indicial roots ${\lambda }_{1}\ge {\lambda }_{2}$ is given by

$$
y={c}_{1}{y}_{1}(x)+{c}_{2}{y}_{2}(x),
$$

where

- ${y}_{1}(x)={x}^{{\lambda }_{1}}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}({\lambda }_{1}){x}^{n}$ is the first Frobenius solution corresponding to the larger root of the indicial equation, and

- ${a}_{n}({\lambda }_{1})$ are the coefficients produced by the method when $\lambda ={\lambda }_{1}.$

We are given that the indicial equation is $2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda =0.$
Solving for the roots, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda (2\lambda -1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =0,\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The larger solution is ${\lambda }_{1}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore, the first Frobenius series solution we take is

$$
{y}_{1}(x)={x}^{1/2}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}.
$$

With $\lambda =\frac{1}{2},$ the recurrence relation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =\frac{5}{(\frac{1}{2}+n)(2(\frac{1}{2}+n)-1)}\,{a}_{n-1} \\  & =\frac{5}{(n+\frac{1}{2})(2n)}\,{a}_{n-1} \\  & =\frac{5}{n(2n+1)}\,{a}_{n-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, with ${a}_{0}\ne 0$ arbitrary, we evaluate the first three coefficients using the given recurrence relation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & \ne 0, \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{5}{1(2\cdot 1+1)}\,{a}_{0}=\frac{5}{3}{a}_{0}, \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{5}{2(2\cdot 2+1)}\,{a}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{3}{a}_{0}=\frac{5}{6}{a}_{0}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the first Frobenius solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}(x) & ={x}^{1/2}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} \\  & ={x}^{1/2}({a}_{0}+\frac{5}{3}{a}_{0}x+\frac{5}{6}{a}_{0}{x}^{2}+⋯) \\  & ={a}_{0}({x}^{1/2}+\frac{5}{3}{x}^{3/2}+\frac{5}{6}{x}^{5/2}+⋯).\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The general solution near a regular singular point x=0 of a second-order homogeneous linear differential equation with indicial roots λ1≥λ2 is given by y=c1y1(x)+c2y2(x), where

  • y1(x)=xλ1∑n=0∞an(λ1)xn is the first Frobenius solution corresponding to the larger root of the indicial equation, and

  • an(λ1) are the coefficients produced by the method when λ=λ1.

We are given that the indicial equation is 2λ2−λ=0. Solving for the roots, we get

2λ2−λ=0λ(2λ−1)=0λ=0,12

The larger solution is λ1=12. Therefore, the first Frobenius series solution we take is

y1(x)=x1/2∑n=0∞anxn.

With λ=12, the recurrence relation is given by

an=5(12+n)(2(12+n)−1)an−1=5(n+12)(2n)an−1=5n(2n+1)an−1.

Now, with a0≠0 arbitrary, we evaluate the first three coefficients using the given recurrence relation as follows:

a0≠0,a1=51(2⋅1+1)a0=53a0,a2=52(2⋅2+1)a1=12⋅53a0=56a0.

Therefore, the first Frobenius solution is

y1(x)=x1/2∑n=0∞anxn=x1/2(a0+53a0x+56a0x2+⋯)=a0(x1/2+53x3/2+56x5/2+⋯).
